title: ESP32-C6 upstream refresh A/B at kixel-ai/rind `8a5977ad`
board: ESP32-C6 rev v0.2, 4 MB flash, USB-Serial/JTAG; the board whose MAC ends 2C:48

toolchain.rustc: rustc 1.98.1 (nixpkgs), riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf, opt-level 3, lto fat, codegen-units 1

harness: WS-BENCH firmware for the C6 (private harness, not published here): ChaCha20-Poly1305 seal/open and Ed25519 for rind and RustCrypto/dalek, plus rind-only AES-128-GCM seal/open and P-256 sign/verify. Rows are medians of 32 calls (8 for Ed25519 and P-256).
note: Control of an interleaved A/B on one ESP32-C6. Each run is one flash of c6-ctl.bin; the run's value is the median over that boot's complete rounds. Variants are in ab.json.

ctl.what: kixel-ai/rind main 8a5977ad as it is (HACL* ChaCha20 rounds and 64-byte keystream array, HACL* Poly1305 in u64 limbs, aws-lc bitsliced AES, 64-bit-product GHASH, 6-bit P-256 table, byte-at-a-time volatile key wipe)

zero.what: + key wipe as one memset on riscv32

aes.what: + fixsliced AES and a mulhu-free GHASH on 32-bit portable

cp.what: + 26-bit Poly1305 and word-XOR ChaCha20 on riscv32

all.what: zero + aes + p256 + cp together (on top of #297)

results_intro: Interleaved A/B of five fork branches against upstream [kixel-ai/rind](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind) main [`8a5977ad`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/8a5977adb9c32ea2ed010c400f5ffbdcdec14b47) on one ESP32-C6, 2026-11-23. The tables below are the control image, six flashes. [ab.md](ab.md) has every image against the control, [RUNS.md](RUNS.md) every control run, and [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) the method and what each image is.
results_ab: [ab.md](ab.md): each candidate image (`zero`, `aes`, `p256`, `cp`, `all`) was flashed once, between two control flashes. One flash is one run, so the candidates do not meet the three-run rule; see [NOTES.md](NOTES.md).
